Configuration géométrique qui empêche le: Geometric configuration that stops hydrocarbons from migrating further and holds them (anticline, sealing fault, stratigraphic pinch-out, salt dome flank).
Roche poreuse et perméable capable de st: Porous and permeable rock able to store hydrocarbons and let them flow (sandstone, fractured or karstified limestone).
Roche imperméable au-dessus du réservoir: Impermeable rock above the reservoir that blocks vertical migration of hydrocarbons (thick clay, evaporite).
Apport en hydrocarbures au piège, par mi: Supply of hydrocarbons to the trap, by migration from a mature source rock (kitchen). Without charge, a perfect trap stays empty.
Zone de roche-mère suffisamment mature p: Zone of source rock mature enough to actively generate hydrocarbons, at a given moment in the basin's history.
Déplacement des hydrocarbures depuis la: Movement of hydrocarbons from the source rock to the trap, driven by buoyancy: they preferentially migrate toward the nearest structural high.
Stade de transformation de la matière or: Stage of transformation of organic matter into hydrocarbons, driven by the temperature reached during deepest burial, not by present depth.
Remontée et érosion d'un bassin depuis s: Uplift and erosion of a basin since its maximum burial. A strongly exhumed basin can have a mature source rock at shallow present depth.
Pli convexe vers le haut ; un des pièges: Upward-convex fold; one of the most classic structural traps when combined with a continuous seal.
Fracture with vertical offset of the layers. It can seal a trap (juxtaposition against an impermeable layer) or, conversely, let hydrocarbons leak.
Amincissement progressif puis disparitio: Gradual thinning then lateral disappearance of a layer, creating a stratigraphic trap with no need for deformation.
Remontée diapirique de sel qui déforme l: Diapiric rise of salt that deforms the surrounding layers and creates traps on its flanks.
Position relative d'un point par rapport: Relative position of a point compared with the other blocks of the map in terms of reservoir depth: a structural high is a point where the reservoir is relatively shallow (often more favourable to trapping).
La porosité mesure le volume de vide pou: Porosity measures the void volume able to store fluids; permeability measures the ability of those fluids to flow. A good reservoir needs both.
Étude régionale bon marché qui révèle la: Cheap regional study that reveals the general structure (structural highs/lows) of the whole concession in a single campaign.
Profil le long d'un transect A→B qui rév: Profile along an A→B transect that reveals the geometry of the horizons and the faults along this profile.
